findings: One outstanding task still stalls: queue concurrency is not required in the reproduced published-host failure.
Measured synchronous createImageBitmap call and main-thread drawImage readback each take roughly ten seconds; the remaining Promise settlement takes milliseconds in the captured sample.
The script-free native host in the intermediate boundary run also records a ten-second canvas readback despite an eventual-pixel pass. Green result alone is insufficient to infer no stall.
The final diagnostic bounds readback durations at seven seconds across initial playback, seek and layout. This opt-in bound does not change production defaults.
Idle readback passes once but changes observation scheduling. It is not a demonstrated runtime fix or evidence that screenshot/JASSUB failures have been resolved.
limitations: No native stack, lock identity or exact browser root cause; no offscreen-default change, vendor patch, publication, physical-device or full-package acceptance.
Worker and main-thread performance clocks have different origins. Durations are compared within each realm, not by subtracting cross-realm timestamps.
Early source revisions differ as explicitly identified. Final source fingerprints only cover final/idle/fillRect runs. Raw traces remain local.
Windows WebKit lacks canvas transfer; its cases exercise main-thread fillRect, not ImageBitmap or offscreen rendering.
